newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian PM worried by possible Lyonnaise, Suez deal.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM worried by possible Lyonnaise, Suez deal.

text.p: Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Friday he was concerned about the effects on Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA of a possible merger between French Compagnie de Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux.
Dehaene said he had told Suez chief Gerard Mestrallet the government was particularly anxious that Tractebel should retain its autonomy if Suez and Lyonnaise did merge.

"For us this is of prime concern," Dehaene told reporters after the weekly cabinet meeting, adding that Mestrallet understood. "There is also a question over whether there would have to be a public offer."
Economics Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Elio di Rupo voiced stronger sentiments on Wednesday.

He said a merger would harm Belgian interests since it would affect the strategy of Belgian holding company SGB, and thus of its unit Tractebel and Tractebel's own units, notably those operating in the energy sector in Belgium and abroad. Suez owns 63 percent of SGB.
Tractebel is mainly active in electricity production and gas distribution, while Lyonnaise is mainly active in water. Both groups are active in waste management.
In recent years Tractebel has repeatedly met political resistance in Belgium because through SGB it is French-owned.
Tractebel parent SGB controls key sectors of the Belgian economy including banking, energy, insurance and several blue-chip industrial companies.
